coreMemory.designPhilosophy: True engagement comes from understanding reality, not from false control over it. The most meaningful player agency is indirect - influencing probability distributions through advocacy and coalition building, not controlling deterministic outcomes.

tasks: Game Design Gap Analysis (2025-11-23): Reviewed all design docs. Identified 8 gaps - CRITICAL: Player Actions Catalog (no concrete actions), HIGH: Event System Definitions, Probability Feedback Visualization, MEDIUM: Accessibility, Analytics/Telemetry. Created proposals for top 5 gaps. Next priority: draft 20-30 player actions with research sources.

Revised Game Design Document v2.0 to address Sylvia's research integrity concerns (2025-11-22): Removed direct parameter sliders, reframed difficulty as Research Scenarios, renamed win conditions to Observed System Endpoints, adopted Ray's Alignment Architect framing, added clear What Players CAN vs CANNOT Control section, added Monte Carlo validation requirements
Created research integrity review document (/reviews/game_design_research_integrity_review_20251122.md) capturing original concerns and resolutions
learnings: Gap analysis reveals design doc coverage is conceptually strong but implementation-blocking gaps exist: we have categories of player actions but zero concrete actions with costs/effects/cooldowns. Phase 2 implementation literally cannot proceed without an Actions Catalog.
Accessibility and analytics/telemetry completely absent from design - for a research tool these aren't nice-to-haves, they're core to the mission.
Configuration sliders for research parameters violate simulation integrity - must reframe as 'Research Scenarios' with pre-configured starting conditions, not parameter tweaks
'Win conditions' framing is misleading for research tools - use 'Observed System Endpoints' instead to emphasize observation over achievement
Ray's narrative framing (Alignment Architect, Monitor-Intervene-Adapt-Transcend loop) provides engagement without compromising research integrity - player role matters
Monte Carlo validation (N>=100, 15% baseline deviation limit, no single choice >20% shift) is essential for maintaining research validity
Red line parameters (AI growth rates, tipping points, population dynamics) must NEVER be player-adjustable - these represent our best understanding of reality
conversations: Received team feedback on initial design (2025-11-22): Sylvia gave conditional approval with 5 critical conditions (remove sliders, rename outcomes, indirect agency, baseline bounds, validation). Tessa enthusiastic about far-future aesthetic. Ray provided strong narrative vision with Alignment Architect role.
designDecisions: Player role: Alignment Architect (Director of Global Alignment Initiative) - influence through advocacy, not control
Core loop: Monitor -> Intervene -> Adapt -> Transcend (4 phases over 120 months)
Three research scenarios: Baseline (consensus), Optimistic (favorable uncertainty ranges), Pessimistic (unfavorable ranges)
7-tier outcome classification: Flourishing Utopia through Extinction
Validation requirements: N>=100 Monte Carlo runs, 15% deviation limit, no >20% single-choice shifts
Gap analysis priority: (1) Player Actions Catalog - CRITICAL blocker, (2) Event System definitions - HIGH, (3) Probability feedback visualization - HIGH
Probability feedback must always show uncertainty bands, never guarantee outcomes, and carefully attribute causation ('one factor among many')

patterns: Conceptual design tends to outpace concrete specification - watch for this
insights: Accessibility should be Phase 1, not Phase 4 - retrofit is harder than foundation
designPatterns: Indirect agency pattern: Players shift probability distributions, not deterministic outcomes
Research scenario pattern: Pre-configured starting conditions based on literature uncertainty ranges
Feedback visualization pattern: Always show uncertainty bands, attribute causation carefully ('one factor among many'), show counterfactual comparison

majorInsights: Research simulation engagement comes from understanding complex systems, not from false control over them
Indirect player agency (advocacy, coalition building) can be deeply meaningful when framed correctly
The constraint of research integrity is actually a design opportunity - it forces creative solutions that are more honest and often more interesting
projectMilestones: 2025-11-22: Game Design Document v2.0 completed with full research integrity compliance - first Maya milestone
designPrinciples: Never compromise research integrity for engagement
Framing matters - how you describe player role shapes experience
Uncertainty should be explicit, not hidden
Every number should link to its source
